Fascicle Two. By stating the property of the subject and the forward and backward pervasions, the certainty of the forward and backward pervasions is also explained, and the certainty of the property of the subject is also explained. The forward and backward pervasions, which have the same method of ascertainment, are distinguished from the property of the subject and taught. It is not the meaning here that "forward and backward pervasions are also explained." Where realizing one thing results in realizing another, it is appropriate to state it like this; but when something states only that thing, having explained it, to state it again like this would be meaningless. If one asks, "Is realizing the pervasion by that property also the purpose of stating it?" No, because by saying "pervasion is..." and so on, just as its nature is stated, they are realized in that way. What other realization is there in the property of the subject itself, that it would be stated "the property of the subject is also explained"? Therefore, even though taught without explicitly mentioning certainty, it is precisely the statement of certainty itself that is established here. If one asks what kind of certainty is here, in order to summarize those three modes where it exists, it says "those": the property of the subject and its pervasion by that property are the three reasons having the characteristics of effect, nature, and non-observation. When illustrating the three signs as stated with examples, explaining the three, effect and so on, as "like this and this" is from "for example" up to "is explained." Thus, following the stated order, first the effect is established, second is the nature. Lastly is non-observation. Setting out both the reason and the probandum is for the sake of establishing the very nature of cause and effect. The reason of nature is "because it is a <term>śiṃśapā</term> <gloss>a type of tree</gloss> tree." Here too, establishing both is for the sake of demonstrating it precisely as a reason of nature, because those two are established as being of one nature.

Therefore, this is cognized only by something else as a cognizer. The thought that "that exists even in an illuminating lamp" is answered by: "But being cognized by another is like form and so forth." The objection that "Even happiness is cognized only by another, because it is an object of cognition" is stated as: "Being something else."

The answer is "being something else." Since blue, happiness, and all such things are cognized only by something else, consciousness would be non-existent.

To the thought, "Is it not cognized by something else that apprehends happiness and so forth, either through implicit understanding or by direct perception arising from the contact between the self and the mind?" it is stated: "For whom there is cognition." The meaning is that if everything appears as an object of cognition, it is contradictory for it to be a cognizer.

But if it is cognized by that which contacts it, what is that? It is not the body and so forth, nor is it happiness, because it is an object of cognition. It is not something else, because it does not appear. This is taught by: "Happiness, blue, and so forth."

"It may be true that it does not appear, but it is understood." To this, it is said that while being understood, it is not a logical reason, like a rabbit's horn.

Its non-existence is taught by: "The eye and so forth." The consciousness of happiness and so forth is not logical as something else, so it is imagined as a mind that is the transformation of the self, whose nature is the activity of the eye and so forth. Therefore, to the thought that it is taught as having no logical reason, it is said: "Through the effect."

How could the very thing that is the logical reason of the effect's consciousness be the object to be proven? This is taught by: "That too is potency."

If the eye and so forth have the activity of form and so forth, they have a temporary nature, and that consciousness will not arise later. Therefore, it is understood as a nature of transformation existing in the sense faculty or existing in the self, and that is potency. This thought is: "The state of observation."

There they are seen clearly in the forms. 
The meaning of the word that acts as knowledge 
Is not external in any way. 
Because it is not an object that exists otherwise, 
If this very intention to speak 
Is proven to be the cause of understanding, 
It is extremely clear in the third defining characteristic. 

If the intention to speak has not become manifest, 
The word does not connect. 
A lamp itself, regarding blue and so forth, 
Is not what causes knowledge from being a sign. 
What is suitable to generate knowledge 
Is said to be so because it arises. 
If it is the reality of a sign that causes knowledge, 
Consider the property of the subject and so forth. 
Otherwise, regarding a person and so forth like that, 
Why is there no dispute? 
Why not establish what is apprehended by the eye 
As something that is not feasible otherwise? 
Because it lacks the property of the subject, 
Therefore, having one defining characteristic is inferior. 
Whatever has one mode that is stated 
Indicates having two modes. 
By stating those with two modes, 
Through the property of the subject, it has three modes. 
If you think it is implied by being not feasible otherwise, 
That is not so. 
Otherwise, even for sound and so forth, 
This very apprehension by the eye is accepted. 
The reason "because he is his son" and so forth, 
Because it is not contradictory to the discordant class, 
Since the reversal is in doubt, 
Those three modes do not exist. 
Even if he is the son of that son, 
Due to the division of causes of karma and food and so forth, 
In all cases, 
The entity will be different. 
This is not an effect or an intrinsic nature, 
Nor is it the non-apprehension of an appearance. 
If it is not different from that, 
It would be infallible. 
If infallibility 
Is seen even in other things, 
For example, regarding the opening of night lotuses and so forth 
And the rising of the ocean, 
The rising of the moon is the sign; 
And from seeing the presence of the tormentor, 
One fully knows the presence of a shadow 
In other parts. 
By seeing a burnt piece of wood in the dark, 
One infers smoke from afar. 
Also from the rising of the Pleiades, 
One understands the proximity of Aldebaran. 
In this, that property of the reason 
Is understood like that.
